amortization_base.engine_limitation_note: ENGINE LIMITATION -- READ BEFORE RELYING ON THE GENERATED SCHEDULE'S scheduled_principal FIGURES. The Credit Agreement's own wording ('0.60% of beginning principal FOR THE APPLICABLE MONTH') and the borrower's own monthly Debt & Liquidity schedules (in every Monthly_Financial_Package and every Covenant_Calculation workbook reviewed) both confirm this is a DECLINING-BALANCE (self-amortizing) mechanic: 0.60% is applied to that month's OWN opening balance, so the dollar amortization shrinks every month (e.g. certified Scheduled Principal $152,219.84 in 2025-07 declining to $142,469.36 by 2026-06, each exactly 0.60% of that month's own beginning balance). debt_service.py v1's amortization_base concept instead computes the base as 'the aggregate original principal of all fundings dated strictly before the payment date' -- a value that is FIXED absent a new draw -- which produces a FLAT, level monthly installment (0.60% x $26,302,782.34 = $157,816.69 every month) rather than the true shrinking one. The generated schedule below is therefore NOT expected to tie to the borrower's certified monthly scheduled-principal figures from month 2 onward, and the gap widens every month (by 2026-06 the engine's cumulative scheduled principal paid since first payment, ~$2,840,700, is about $140,000 (~5%) higher than the certified cumulative reduction of ~$2,700,358 over the same 18 months). This is an engine capability gap (no declining-balance amortization base is supported in v1), not a data-entry error -- see the return-level ambiguity for the two paths forward (accept the flat approximation and reconcile scheduled_principal to the certificates by hand each month, or hold this row until the engine supports a declining base).

analyst_decision.decision: Do NOT rely on this generated schedule's 'scheduled_principal' / balloon figures for Nemeris. Until debt_service.py supports a true declining-balance amortization base, build-monitoring-model and the covenant/three-statement modules should read the borrower's own certified Debt & Liquidity tab (Beginning Debt / Draws / PIK / Scheduled Principal / Ending Debt) for actual monthly principal paid and outstanding balance -- that tab already ties to every certificate exactly. This generated schedule's cash_interest figures are a reasonable approximation (interest is on a materially similar declining base either way, and the discrepancy compounds much more slowly there), but should also be cross-checked against the certified TTM Covenant EBITDA / Net Debt figures each quarter rather than trusted blind.

ambiguities: The Credit Agreement says only 'actual days elapsed over a 360-day year' -- it does not state, in so many words, whether both the first and last day of an accrual period are counted. count_both_endpoints is set to true here because that is the reading that makes a FULL calendar month count its true number of calendar days (e.g. 31 for January), which is the standard actual/360 bank-loan convention and is consistent with 'actual days elapsed'. The reading is untested at the one place it actually matters: the funding-month stub (January 15-31, 2025 -- 17 days inclusive vs. 16 days exclusive) and the maturity stub (through January 15, 2030). Neither stub is large enough to move the Net Leverage Ratio, but it does move the exact cash-interest cent amount in those two months. Recorded for step-7 sign-off; alternative reading is count_both_endpoints: false (16-day / exclusive stub).

_fees_not_modeled_note: The executed Fee Letter states a 1.50% closing fee (of funded commitments, one-time, at close) and a $75,000 ANNUAL administration fee -- confirmed against the Fee Letter and consistent with the Credit Agreement (Section 3.02: 'Closing, administrative and unused commitment fees are governed by the executed Fee Letter'). Neither is modeled in the 'fees' array above: the engine's fees.when enum supports only 'close_and_payment_dates' (fires at close AND at every MONTHLY payment date for the life of the loan), 'payment_dates' (every month), or 'maturity' (once, at the end) -- there is no 'one-time at close' or 'annual' cadence. Modeling the 1.50% closing fee under 'close_and_payment_dates' would incorrectly repeat ~$394,541.74 every month for 60 months instead of charging it once; modeling the $75,000 annual admin fee the same way would repeat $75,000 every month instead of once a year. Rather than generate a fee schedule that is silently and dramatically wrong, both fees are omitted here and flagged for the analyst / engine owner (see the run's ambiguities list). Neither fee is a covenant Fixed Charge in this agreement in any case -- both would carry fixed_charges_treatment 'excluded' if modeled. ALSO NOTE: the Credit Agreement cross-references the Fee Letter for an 'unused commitment fee' on the undrawn $8,697,217.66 DDTL commitment (Section 3.02), but the executed Fee Letter itself states only the closing fee and the annual administration fee -- no unused/undrawn commitment fee rate appears anywhere in the four-page executed Fee Letter, the Credit Agreement, or the Final IC Memo. This looks like a genuine documentation gap (the CA promises a fee the Fee Letter does not deliver), not an additive reconciling term -- flagged as an ambiguity.

index_rates.source: ASSUMPTION, not a document in the deal folder: approximate 1-month Term SOFR level at the Closing Date, based on the publicly published SOFR level following the Federal Reserve's December 2024 policy action (target range 4.25%-4.50%). None of the executed documents (Credit Agreement, Fee Letter, First Amendment) or the monitoring package states an actual observed Adjusted Term SOFR print or cites a rate notice -- the Credit Agreement's own definition points to 'the rate notice' (Article I, 'Adjusted Term SOFR') as the source of record, and no rate notice is in the deal folder. This single pinned observation is held FLAT for the whole schedule by the engine (disclosed in the generated output's assumptions), which is very unlikely to be exactly right for 2026 given intervening Fed policy changes -- replace with the Agent's actual rate-notice prints when available.
